context: WebGL scatterplot rendering 1 million points across 6 Gaussian clusters, with D3 brush interaction and a small inset 2D histogram of the brushed subset; includes Canvas 2D fallback toggle and FPS counter.
first_impression: Visually clean and immediately readable — six clusters pop as distinct colored blobs against a dense gray point cloud, with no perceptual crowding despite the extreme point count.
what_works: The 6-color Tol colorblind-safe palette with 0.35 alpha is well-calibrated for density: clusters accumulate color while the background scatter stays visually subordinate. Cluster separation is strong enough to identify all six groups at a glance without hovering.
what_doesnt: The inset histogram is quite small (200×160px) with 9px axis labels, making it hard to read spatial detail in brushed subsets — it functions more as a count indicator than an analytical view. Axis labels are generic 'X' and 'Y', stripping any semantic meaning from the coordinate space.
